1 // Gandalf advisor — the unforgeable orchestrator-minted commission-id LEDGER (Wave W2a).
2 //
3 // THE MECHANISM the anti-laundering honor-system scaffold (seam/anti-laundering.mjs) was waiting
4 // for. In Increment 1 `resolveCommissionId` could only ever return UNRESOLVABLE_NO_LEDGER — there
5 // was no oracle of authenticity, so the content-binding canaries B2' (a forged / unresolvable
6 // commission-id FAILS) and B7' (a commissioned result is BOUND to the id that produced it) were
7 // stamped BLOCKED-this-cycle and NON-GATING. This module is the real ledger: an orchestrator-minted,
8 // cryptographically-bound commission-id that a random / forged / tampered id can NEVER satisfy.
9 //
10 // Modeled on ramanujan's Wave-4/Wave-9 artifact mint (src/adjudication.mjs `computeNonce` /
11 // `mintArtifact` / `consumeArtifact`): the id is bound to its CONTENT by a keyed hash, and resolve
12 // re-derives that binding from the presented bytes to confirm authenticity — a forged or cross-claim
13 // id fails the re-derivation. Two independent guarantees make an id unforgeable:
14 //   1. CONTENT-BINDING (HMAC). The id embeds the canonical tuple and an HMAC-SHA256 signature over it
15 //      keyed by a per-run secret. Tamper any field (a different result_digest) and the signature no
16 //      longer verifies. Fabricate a random id and it carries no valid signature. Neither can be
17 //      produced without the mint's secret.
18 //   2. MINTED-THIS-RUN (ledger membership). resolve additionally requires the id to have actually
19 //      been minted by THIS ledger this run — an id from a different run/secret is rejected even if it
20 //      were otherwise well-formed. This is the durable "orchestrator-minted, resolvable" property.
21 //
22 // Stdlib-only (node:crypto), deterministic-testable: within one process, mint->resolve round-trips
23 // exactly; a forged/random/tampered/cross-ledger id deterministically resolves to null.
24 //
25 // Public surface:
26 //   COMMISSION_ID_PREFIX               — the versioned id prefix ('gcl1')
27 //   canonicalCommissionTuple(tuple)    — the exact bytes the signature binds (fixed key order)
28 //   createCommissionLedger({secret?})  — an isolated ledger { mintCommission, resolveCommission, ... }
29 //   mintCommission(tuple)              — mint on the module-default per-run ledger
30 //   resolveCommission(id)              — resolve on the module-default per-run ledger
31 //   resetLedger()                      — clear + rotate the module-default ledger for cross-run reuse
32 
33 import crypto from 'node:crypto';
34 
35 /** The versioned commission-id prefix (gandalf-commission-ledger v1). */
36 export const COMMISSION_ID_PREFIX = 'gcl1';
37 
38 // The segment delimiter. A literal '.' is absent from the base64url alphabet (A-Za-z0-9-_), from the
39 // lowercase-hex signature (0-9a-f), and from the prefix 'gcl1', so an id splits back into its three
40 // parts unambiguously.
41 const SEP = '.';
42 
43 function isNonEmptyString(v) {
44   return typeof v === 'string' && v.trim() !== '';
45 }
46 
47 /** The canonical, stable serialization of the bound tuple (FIXED key order) — the exact bytes the
48  *  HMAC signs, so mint and resolve agree byte-for-byte regardless of caller key order. Pure. */
49 export function canonicalCommissionTuple({ drafter_family, refuter_family, result_digest } = {}) {
50   return JSON.stringify({
51     drafter_family: String(drafter_family),
52     refuter_family: String(refuter_family),
53     result_digest: String(result_digest),
54   });
55 }
56 
57 function isWellFormedTuple(t) {
58   return (
59     t !== null &&
60     typeof t === 'object' &&
61     !Array.isArray(t) &&
62     isNonEmptyString(t.drafter_family) &&
63     isNonEmptyString(t.refuter_family) &&
64     isNonEmptyString(t.result_digest)
65   );
66 }
67 
68 function b64urlEncode(str) {
69   return Buffer.from(str, 'utf8').toString('base64url');
70 }
71 function b64urlDecode(str) {
72   return Buffer.from(str, 'base64url').toString('utf8');
73 }
74 
75 function hmacHex(secret, msg) {
76   return crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(msg, 'utf8').digest('hex');
77 }
78 
79 /** Constant-time equality of two equal-length hex strings; false (never throws) on any mismatch of
80  *  type or length so a forged signature cannot leak timing OR crash resolve. */
81 function timingSafeHexEqual(a, b) {
82   if (typeof a !== 'string' || typeof b !== 'string' || a.length !== b.length || a.length === 0) {
83     return false;
84   }
85   try {
86     return crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(a, 'utf8'), Buffer.from(b, 'utf8'));
87   } catch {
88     return false;
89   }
90 }
91 
92 /**
93  * Create an ISOLATED commission ledger backed by a per-run secret. Each ledger mints ids only its own
94  * `resolveCommission` will honor (content-binding secret + minted-this-run membership). Pass an
95  * explicit `secret` for a reproducible fixture; omit it for a fresh random per-run secret.
96  *
97  * @param {{secret?: string|Buffer}} [opts]
98  * @returns {{ mintCommission: Function, resolveCommission: Function, isMinted: Function, size: Function }}
99  */
100 export function createCommissionLedger({ secret } = {}) {
101   let runSecret =
102     secret != null
103       ? Buffer.from(secret instanceof Buffer ? secret : String(secret), 'utf8')
104       : crypto.randomBytes(32);
105   const issued = new Set(); // ids minted by THIS ledger this run
106 
107   /**
108    * Mint a commission-id CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY BOUND to (drafter_family, refuter_family, result_digest).
109    * The id = `gcl1.base64url(canonicalTuple).HMAC-SHA256(secret, canonicalTuple)` — it cannot be
110    * fabricated for a tuple without the mint's secret. Throws on a malformed tuple (never mints a
111    * partial/forgeable id).
112    *
113    * @param {{drafter_family:string, refuter_family:string, result_digest:string}} tuple
114    * @returns {string} the minted commission-id
115    */
116   function mintCommission({ drafter_family, refuter_family, result_digest } = {}) {
117     const tuple = { drafter_family, refuter_family, result_digest };
118     if (!isWellFormedTuple(tuple)) {
119       throw new Error(
120         'commission-ledger: mintCommission requires non-empty drafter_family, refuter_family, and result_digest strings'
121       );
122     }
123     const payload = canonicalCommissionTuple(tuple);
124     const mac = hmacHex(runSecret, payload);
125     const id = `${COMMISSION_ID_PREFIX}${SEP}${b64urlEncode(payload)}${SEP}${mac}`;
126     issued.add(id);
127     return id;
128   }
129 
130   /**
131    * Resolve a commission-id to the tuple it is bound to, or `null` for any id this ledger did not
132    * authentically mint. Returns null when the id is: not a string / wrong prefix / malformed; carries a
133    * signature that does not re-derive from its embedded tuple (a forged or TAMPERED id — e.g. a swapped
134    * result_digest); or was not minted by THIS ledger this run (a random or cross-run/cross-secret id).
135    *
136    * @param {string} id
137    * @returns {{drafter_family:string, refuter_family:string, result_digest:string} | null}
138    */
139   function resolveCommission(id) {
140     if (typeof id !== 'string' || id.length === 0) return null;
141     const parts = id.split(SEP);
142     if (parts.length !== 3 || parts[0] !== COMMISSION_ID_PREFIX) return null;
143     let payload;
144     try {
145       payload = b64urlDecode(parts[1]);
146     } catch {
147       return null;
148     }
149     // (1) CONTENT-BINDING: re-derive the HMAC over the presented tuple bytes. A forged id or a tampered
150     //     tuple (any field changed) yields a different signature and fails here.
151     const expectedMac = hmacHex(runSecret, payload);
152     if (!timingSafeHexEqual(expectedMac, parts[2])) return null;
153     // (2) MINTED-THIS-RUN: it must have actually been minted by THIS ledger (orchestrator-minted,
154     //     resolvable). An id from another run/secret is rejected even if otherwise well-formed.
155     if (!issued.has(id)) return null;
156     let tuple;
157     try {
158       tuple = JSON.parse(payload);
159     } catch {
160       return null;
161     }
162     if (!isWellFormedTuple(tuple)) return null;
163     return {
164       drafter_family: tuple.drafter_family,
165       refuter_family: tuple.refuter_family,
166       result_digest: tuple.result_digest,
167     };
168   }
169 
170   /** Predicate: was `id` minted by THIS ledger this run? Pure; never throws. */
171   function isMinted(id) {
172     return typeof id === 'string' && issued.has(id);
173   }
174 
175   /** The number of ids minted by this ledger this run. */
176   function size() {
177     return issued.size;
178   }
179 
180   /** Reset the ledger for reuse across runs: clear the minted-this-run membership AND rotate the
181    *  per-run secret. After reset(), every previously-minted id resolves to null (its signature no
182    *  longer re-derives under the new secret AND it is no longer in `issued`) — a clean per-run state
183    *  with no leak from the prior run. Pure side-effect on this closure; returns nothing. */
184   function reset() {
185     issued.clear();
186     runSecret = crypto.randomBytes(32);
187   }
188 
189   return { mintCommission, resolveCommission, isMinted, size, reset };
190 }
191 
192 // The module-default ledger: a single per-run secret minted once at import (never persisted), so a
193 // forged id from any other process/run cannot resolve here. Callers that need an isolated/reproducible
194 // ledger use createCommissionLedger({ secret }).
195 const _defaultLedger = createCommissionLedger();
196 
197 /** Mint a commission-id on the module-default per-run ledger. See createCommissionLedger().mintCommission. */
198 export function mintCommission(tuple) {
199   return _defaultLedger.mintCommission(tuple);
200 }
201 
202 /** Resolve a commission-id on the module-default per-run ledger. See createCommissionLedger().resolveCommission. */
203 export function resolveCommission(id) {
204   return _defaultLedger.resolveCommission(id);
205 }
206 
207 /** Reset the module-default ledger (clear its minted-this-run set + rotate its secret) for any caller
208  *  that must REUSE the singleton across runs without leaking a prior run's minted ids. The runtime host
209  *  (runtime/seam-pass.applySeamPass) does NOT rely on this — it instantiates a FRESH per-run ledger via
210  *  createCommissionLedger() so there is no shared singleton state to leak. See createCommissionLedger().reset. */
211 export function resetLedger() {
212   _defaultLedger.reset();
213 }
